name: Gen1 Upgrade Readiness
description: Read-only post-upgrade acceptance checks: exact migration receipt, separately approved first refresh, destination data/freshness, incremental settings and consumers. Never refresh, take over, grant, rewrite or upgrade automatically.

variables.RECEIPT_ID: Original local upgrade receipt, not an operation trace.
variables.DATAFLOW_ID: Exact upgraded dataflow UUID from the receipt.
variables.FIRST_REFRESH_JOB_ID: Exact job ID retained from a separately approved first refresh; never latest history.
variables.WAREHOUSE_ID: Reviewed Warehouse UUID, only for a Warehouse destination; never an inferred destination.
variables.SQL_ENDPOINT_ID: Reviewed SQL analytics endpoint UUID for a Lakehouse destination (not its Lakehouse ID).
variables.VALIDATION_SQL: Reviewed read-only SELECT checks for exact destination tables, expected batch/row bounds and freshness high-watermarks. Quote identifiers; no DDL/DML, source rows in public logs or arbitrary endpoint changes.
variables.JOB_TYPE: Original reviewed schedule job type, not a guessed value.
variables.MODEL_REFRESH_ID: Exact separately approved downstream refresh request UUID, when required.

prerequisites: Retain the original receipt and pre-upgrade definitions, expected destinations, data checks and incremental-refresh baseline privately.

Upgrade approval is NOT approval to run a first refresh, take ownership, grant permissions or rewrite consumers. If no approved refresh receipt exists, record first_refresh:not_checked and stop the acceptance gate; do not create or select a job automatically.
Use the original configured service endpoint and exact IDs. Missing/partial/error-bearing projections remain unknown; a successful migration or preserved item ID is not operational readiness.

steps.description: Require a scope/count-validated successful migration result for the selected dataflow. Partial or unknown results stop acceptance without replay.
Confirm the exact upgraded item is visible; do not infer data readiness from ID preservation or existence.

Compare destinations, schemas/mappings, names, schedules, linked-query behavior, incremental-refresh/watermark settings and security/storage assumptions against the retained baseline. Missing/hidden settings are unknown, not equal. Do not print connection secrets or modify settings.

Observe only the separately approved first refresh. Require exact identity and Completed with consistent failure evidence; acceptance, timeout or cancellation request is not completion. Do not submit a refresh here.
Compare the complete current schedule inventory to the reviewed baseline. Missing/partial inventory is not proof schedules match; do not create or alter schedules.

Verify approved table schema/row bounds, expected batch or business keys and freshness high-watermarks in the actual Warehouse. Refresh completion alone cannot pass data checks. Empty/stale/malformed/unavailable evidence blocks acceptance; never load or repair data automatically.

steps.applies_when: Reviewed destination is a Lakehouse SQL analytics endpoint
steps.description: Alternative to the Warehouse probe: inspect the selected Lakehouse destination through its actual SQL endpoint UUID with the same reviewed read-only data/freshness checks. Never pass a Lakehouse ID as a Warehouse ID or infer a destination from a similar name.

For each selected consumer, check exact model refresh, schema, selected-table queryability and report binding under the intended reader identity. Replace the illustrative table/minimum with approved expectations. Queryability does not prove freshness or visual/business correctness; verify those separately. Do not change modes, rebind, refresh or grant roles.

acceptance_gate.rule: Record each check as ready, blocked, needs_action, unknown or not_checked with scoped evidence and observation time. Pass only when every applicable check is ready; applicability must come from the reviewed baseline, never from a missing response. Any unknown/not_checked/partial/error fails closed.
acceptance_gate.limitations: This is an acceptance workflow composed from supported observation commands, not an automatic migration/refresh/repair executor. No current tenant fixture or approval is assumed.
